news.title: Dip buyers step back into AI/chip names after the worst week since April 2025
news.text: Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg and TheStreet all report the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq rising this morning with Nvidia and the AI trade back in focus, as investors test whether last week's rout (worst weekly loss since April 2025) is over. Nasdaq futures were climbing into the open; Bloomberg flagged beaten-down shares catching a bid. No single-name driver was found for the watch-list's own gainers (CIEN, GOOGL, META, GNRC, LTM, NOK, ITT, PLTR, CSCO among the largest movers this morning) — read them as part of this broad rebound, not confirmed individual catalysts.

footnotes: QQQ omitted: WebSearch returned conflicting, undated figures (one near $609, one implying a ~$656 Nov 6 close) across repeated attempts — no reconciled, confidently-dated quote was found, so the page carries forward the brief's last confirmed QQQ close (03 Nov, $685.28).

Futures (ES/NQ/YM/RTY) omitted: WebSearch returned mutually inconsistent premarket/early-session percentages from different outlets and times (S&P +0.35% to +0.9%, Nasdaq -0.3% to +0.96% depending on source and snapshot) with no clean two-source match for any single contract, and no figure at all for YM or RTY — publishing an unreconciled number would violate the no-invent rule.
Indices (SPX/DJI/RUT/VIX): FMP's index-quote is a live print read ~12-14 minutes after the 09:30 ET open (open/dayLow/dayHigh already reflect the session so far), not a completed session.

No company-specific driver was found for individual watch-list movers after targeted searches (GOOGL, META, PLTR, CIEN, GNRC, LTM, NOK, ITT, CSCO, AAOI, NTAP among the gainers) — read these as part of the broad AI/chip-led rebound described in the one news item that cleared the two-source bar, not confirmed single-name catalysts.

Only one news item cleared the sourcing bar (3 independent https sources, all dated today) after searches for China-US chip news, Fed/rate-cut odds, oil/energy and specific watch-list names (GOOGL, PLTR, CIEN) returned only stale or undated results — fewer items than the usual 4-6, per the no-invent rule.
